cells.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James discloses that its Traditional Employee affiliation model offers a payout of up to 50% plus a full array of employee benefits.
items.quote:
Model: Traditional Employee
Qualifications*: Minimum 5 years of experience and production qualifications vary.
Payout + Benefits: Up to 50% payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: Raymond James discloses that its Advisor Select affiliation model offers a 70-80% gross payout plus a full array of employee benefits.
items.quote:
Model: Advisor Select
Qualifications*: Minimum 3 years of experience and $3.5 million or higher in annual branch fees and commission revenue.
Payout + Benefits: 70-80% gross payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: Raymond James discloses that its Independent Contractor affiliation model offers an 81% to 90% payout.
items.quote:
Model: Independent Contractor
Qualifications*: Minimum 3 years of experience. Minimum T12 of $150,000 required to join an existing branch and $400,000 to open a new branch.
Payout + Benefits: 81% to 90% payout***.

items.text: Raymond James discloses that its Corporate RIA affiliation model offers an 81% to 90% payout.
items.quote:
Model: Corporate RIA
Qualifications*: Minimum 3 years of experience and $50 million in assets under advisement.
Payout + Benefits: 81% to 90% payout***.

items.text: Raymond James states that independent advisor payouts are higher than employee advisor payouts because independent advisors cover their own overhead costs, and that even on the employee side it has tiered payout systems where production increases move an advisor higher on the payout grid.
items.quote: the independent payouts are higher because they cover their overhead costs... even on the employee side, we have tiered payout systems. And so as production increases, you kind of get higher up on the payout grid as well.

items.text: Raymond James states that its independent contractor financial advisors receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors, because they are generally responsible for all of their direct costs.
items.quote: Our financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.

items.text: Raymond James discloses that a financial advisor can receive a higher portion of the fee paid to the firm depending on the advisor's annual revenue generation with the firm.
items.quote: depending on your financial advisor's annual revenue generation with the Firm, your financial advisor can receive a higher portion of the Fee paid to the Firm (therefore, the Firm retains less of the Fee paid).

cells.reason: The passages state specific payout rates/grids by affiliation model and qualitative descriptions of tiered payouts, so these are facts.
